title: Fostering a Stronger Voice for Students and Staff at Institutes of Higher Learning in Policy-making
what_it_is: Fostering a Stronger Voice for Students and Staff at Institutes of Higher Learning in Policy-making

sections.label: NTU hall allocation dismay
sections.summary: NTU's 2021/2022 hall allocation left international and local students without housing, prompting a 5,500-signature petition urging management to reconsider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To start, there was widespread dismay amongst students at NTU regarding the hall allocation for the 2021/2022 academic year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The release of hall allocation results on the 1 July 2021 left many international students who had been staying on campus throughout due to COVID-19 suddenly homeless and scrambling for alternative lodging before the 15 July deadline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Local students were similarly affected, especially Year One and Year Two students who were supposed to have been guaranteed on-campus housing, according to NTU's guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A petition signed by 5,500 people were set up to urge the management to reconsider their decision.

sections.label: NUS College liberal arts
sections.summary: An early claim that the replacement NUS college would provide liberal arts education was followed by an announcement that liberal arts subjects would likely not be in the core curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There was an early claim that the replacement NUS college would provide a liberal arts education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Then, a later announcement said that liberal arts subjects would likely not be included in the core curriculum, to the surprise of many.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The new NUS College has already admitted Its first students as of August this year.

sections.label: NUS sexual offence punishment
sections.summary: NUS initially prescribed what Miss Baey and many saw as a relatively light punishment for a sexual offence perpetrator, even after her police report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NUS had initially prescribed what was seen by Miss Baey and many as a relatively light punishment for the perpetrator of a sexual offence, even after Miss Baey had made a Police report.

sections.label: Tembusu College opaque process
sections.summary: Prof Tomy Koh said the university had fallen short, as the process was opaque and there was a considerable gap between Dr Fernando's dismissal and Tembusu College being informed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: None other than Prof Tomy Koh, then Rector of Tembusu College, commented that the university had "fallen short ", as the process was opaque and there was a "considerable gap" between the time NUS dismissed Dr Fernando and when the rest of Tembusu College was informed.

sections.label: Top universities adopting practice
sections.summary: At least 13 of the top 50 universities in the latest QS World university rankings have adopted this practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Already, at least 13 of the top 50 universities in the latest QS World university rankings from Hong Kong, North America, Europe and Australia have adopted this practice.

sections.label: NUS fossil fuel divestment petition
sections.summary: Two student groups met NUS administrators after six months, but were told their petition with nearly 800 signatures did not show substantial support for divestment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In March 2019, these two student groups calling on NUS to divest from fossil fuels were granted a meeting with NUS administrators after making such a request for six months, only to be told that their petition, which had garnered nearly 800 signatures, was not enough to show substantial support for divestment.

sections.label: Peer support programme student response
sections.summary: The student response to the peer support programme has generally been supportive, with 1,200 qualified peer helpers and 200 trained yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the impact on employability and other standardised metrics of peer support, may not be clear, talking to students and studying feedback on this programme, I think it is clear that the student response has generally been supportive of the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are now 1,200 qualified peer helpers, with 200 helpers being trained each year.

sections.label: Sharing best practices among IHLs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests sharing best practices among IHLs on feedback handling, accountability and campus experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think some degree of collective experience sharing would help codify how IHLs take in and act on student and staff feedback on issues related to sexual misconduct and other types of issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, in addition to my earlier proposals, I would like to suggest that more be done to share best practices among IHLs and encourage levelling up, particularly in regard to the domains of feedback handling, accountability and the campus experience of students and staff that I have talked about today.

sections.label: Accountability to diverse student groups
sections.summary: The speaker says accountability means fair consideration of holistic demands across diverse students and generations, not just one group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: What we certainly agree with is that we have and we will continue to enhance the accountability and also the participation of faculty and staff in all our institutions – from Government to the IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I think we can all agree on that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But where we are a bit more nuanced than Mr Leon Perera's presentation is this – accountability by the leadership must mean the following; not just accountability to a certain group of students to meet what they desire or want.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Accountability must mean a fair consideration of the holistic demands across the diversity of students, not only in this generation, not only a select group of stakeholders, but for this generation, across diverse student groups and across different generations.

sections.label: Nanyang Polytechnic Student Senate
sections.summary: Nanyang Polytechnic has a Student Senate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In Nanyang Polytechnic, they have a Student Senate.

sections.label: Taking every feedback seriously
sections.summary: The speaker says every issue and feedback is taken seriously regardless of whether it reaches a certain number threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second thing – petitions to be taken seriously set above a certain number.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In fact, the correct thing for us to do, and as what we have been doing, is that we take every issue, every feedback seriously, regardless of whether it has reached a certain threshold of numbers.

sections.label: Considering diverse stakeholders in decisions
sections.summary: The speaker asks how to make the best decision for diverse stakeholders and generations, not just individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Listen to every feedback seriously, give it due consideration and ask ourselves: how do we make the best decision, not just for the individuals who say so, but for the diverse stakeholders in the university compound and ecosystem, and the diverse stakeholders across different generations?

sections.label: Safe space for student debate
sections.summary: The debate states students need a safe space to interact and debate, but not for interest groups that impinge on other groups' interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Just as the debate has said, this must be a safe space for students to interact, to debate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But it cannot be a space whereby you set up any interest group that impinges on the interests of other groups.

sections.label: Autonomous universities accountability and leadership
sections.summary: Six AUs meet to share best practices and work as one Team Singapore, while IHL leadership must exercise responsibility and explain decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, our six AUs, the Presidents and the Chairs of their boards, meet regularly to share the best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And not just to share the best practices but on how they can work as an integrated team to compete as one Team Singapore, rather than competing amongst themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, Sir, I thank Mr Leon Perera for his various suggestions and will take them to heart seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I will emphasise this: accountability means the understanding of diverse stakeholders' interests, not just in the current ecosystem but also across generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And I expect the leadership of the IHLs to exercise their leadership responsibilities to make sensible decisions on what are the things to consult and what are the things that they cannot consult everyone on, but have to take on that leadership responsibility to decide and subsequently, explain those decisions clearly to their people.
